title: Introduce version lockfile, transactional restore playbook, and preflight migration checks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a deterministic version lockfile for installer artifacts, a transactional restore playbook with validated preflight checks, and Helm/Terraform hooks to avoid partial upgrades. Improves rollback safety during schema migrations.
body:
Summary: This PR adds a version.lock file for all private-installer artifacts, implements a transactional restore playbook (scripts/restore/transactional-restore.sh and docs/upgrade-playbooks/transactional-restore.md), and wires preflight migration checks into the Helm chart and Terraform module. Motivation: we've seen two incidents where partial upgrade + schema drift left clusters in an unrecoverable state. The goal is to make upgrades and rollbacks deterministic and testable: (1) pin installer components to exact build artifacts, (2) validate cluster state before applying migrations, and (3) ensure restore is atomic and auditable.

Change highlights (single-line sections kept in one string):
- Version lockfile: added installer/version.lock (SHA256, artifact URLs, build metadata). The install CLI (bin/installer) now consumes the lockfile to ensure deterministic manifests for a given release.
- Transactional restore: scripts/restore/transactional-restore.sh implements a three-phase restore: snapshot-verify -> apply-in-temp-namespace -> promotion-or-rollback. The script is idempotent and logs to /var/log/redwood/restore-<runid>.log.
- Helm chart hooks: charts/redwood-private/templates/preflight-job.yaml adds a pre-upgrade Job that validates KV schema versions, DB migration state, and PV health. The hooks enforce --wait semantics and fail fast with human-readable diagnostics.
- Terraform module changes: terraform/modules/installer/main.tf adds null_resource triggers for snapshot exports and a remote-exec that uploads the lockfile to the state bucket before upgrades.
- Docs and playbooks: docs/upgrade-playbooks/transactional-restore.md and docs/upgrade-playbooks/preflight-checklist.md describe runbooks and recovery timelines; includes a checklist for SREs and customer operators.
- Tests: e2e/installer/restore_integration_test.go adds a simulated partial-upgrade scenario; unit tests added for the lockfile parser. CI fuzzing on malformed lockfiles was added to the pipeline.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological):
- Ankit Rao (2025-11-05): "Love the idea of a single source-of-truth for installer artifacts. Can we ensure the lockfile generation is part of CI artifacts so users can reproduce exact installs? Also request an audit log entry for restore runs."
- Maya Patel (author) reply (2025-11-05): "Yes — CI now uploads the lockfile alongside release artifacts and we add a restore audit event to the operator logs. See commit 1a9b3f2 and transactional-restore.sh logging lines."
- Evelyn Chu (2025-11-06): "Preflight job looks good; add a guard so it does not run on air-gapped installs that cannot access external registries."
- Maya Patel reply (2025-11-06): "Added preflight.skipOnAirgap boolean and documented behavior in README. Preflight will only perform local checks if skipOnAirgap=true."
- Ben Harper (2025-11-08): "Can we make the Terraform upload idempotent to avoid race conditions in CI? Also validate the state bucket permissions must be present before any apply."
- Maya Patel reply (2025-11-09): "Implemented checks using null_resource triggers and remote-exec guards; added permission validation in terraform/modules/installer/README.md."
- Evelyn Chu (2025-11-10) approval comment: "Approved after the airgap changes and additional tests. Please squash on merge."

CI: initial run failed due to flakiness in the integration test (timeout on slow runner). Reran with increased test timeout and all checks passed. CI summary: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), helm-template (pass), terraform-plan (pass), security-scan (pass).

Testing and verification performed:
- Local: validated lockfile consumption with bin/installer --dry-run against a temp cluster (kind).
- Integration: restore_integration_test simulates partial upgrade then runs transactional-restore.sh and asserts cluster state equals pre-upgrade snapshot.
- Manual QA: SRE runbook executed on staging with recovery window < 18 minutes for our standard 3-node cluster.

Rollback story: The transactional restore playbook will create a promotion marker only after the temporary namespace full health checks succeed. If any step fails the playbook triggers an automatic rollback to previous snapshot with explicit logging and an optional operator-confirm step. Helm/Terraform changes ensure the lockfile is preserved in remote state to match the manifest set used during restore.

Operational notes for on-call:
- Look for logs in /var/log/redwood/restore-<runid>.log and audit events under k8s resources labeled redwood.restore.
- Run preflight checks manually with: helm template charts/redwood-private --values values.yaml --set preflight.runLocal=true | kubectl apply -f - --dry-run=client
- If a restore fails mid-run, follow docs/upgrade-playbooks/transactional-restore.md -> Recovery -> manual-fallback for operator-led rollback.

Documentation: added a new page that describes the lockfile schema, the expected lifecycle during upgrades, and how to reproduce a restore locally. Included a troubleshooting section covering common causes of preflight failures (PV attachment, DB schema mismatch, insufficient IAM perms).

Merge: squashed and merged by Evelyn Chu on 2025-11-12 (merge_commit f3b9a8d, method: squash).

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-2245):
- Automate lockfile generation in the release pipeline and publish checksums to the release page.
- Add automated chaos tests that exercise partial upgrade + restore paths.
- Provide a lightweight UI in the console to visualize restore runs and their audit traces.

Notes on uniqueness: This PR focuses on a coordinated lockfile + transactional restore flow and preflight guards wired across Helm and Terraform. It intentionally avoids previous approaches that relied solely on snapshot-based rollbacks by testing promotion semantics before state flip.

If any reviewer wants an expanded walkthrough, I can schedule a 30-minute runbook demo and walkthrough in #sre-ops.
